newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bids $63, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bids $63, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bids early Thursday at $63.00 per cwt were light and passed by owners pricing cattle $64.00 to $65.00, feedlot sources said.

Active sales last Friday and Tuesday, along with a hefty percentage of previously contracted or formulated cattle, pushed movement in Kansas to a record weekly high of 137,700 head, feedlot and USDA sources said.
Sales on Wednesday were light and attributed to "clean-up" activity, one Texas Panhandle source said.
Panhandle weekly movement also was chunky near 134,000 head, but not large enough to bust records.
This week's large cattle movement sold out showlists from a week ago and most of this week, along with part of next week's list, several feedlot sources said.

However, showlists were seen steady to larger compared with this week as cattle supplies continue to expand, they said. Active placements of cattle onto feedlots late last winter and this spring were seen resulting in larger numbers of market-ready cattle well into the summer, the sources said.
Beef prices sagged, but lower prices encouraged sturdy movement. Beef prices Wednesday were quoted down $0.72 to $0.91 per cwt, with 310 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported.
